questions.q: What does the summary say true belonging is mostly about?
a: Learning to belong to yourself first
Being accepted by the largest possible group
Avoiding any situation where you stand alone
Changing your opinions to match your friends
questions.why: The overview says Brown sees belonging as something we mostly owe ourselves, even when nobody is standing behind us.

questions.q: What did Brown start doing to stop depending on other people's opinions?
a: Writing herself permission slips to be herself
Cutting off contact with her old friends
Copying the dress code of her colleagues
Asking her partner to make her decisions
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes permission slips such as allowing herself to be goofy and enjoy life, which made her less reliant on approval.

questions.q: Which trait is part of the seven that build trust, according to the summary?
a: Owning your mistakes openly
Never admitting when you are wrong
Keeping every thought to yourself
Avoiding promises to other people
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists reliability, owning mistakes, respecting boundaries, protecting secrets, integrity, not judging and generosity.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend doing with anger?
a: Acknowledge it and turn it into positive change
Suppress it until the feeling fades away
Let it harden into lasting resentment
Express it only toward people you trust
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to acknowledge anger but use it to become better rather than bitter, before it turns into resentment.

questions.q: What did Antoine Leiris do after losing his wife in the Paris attacks?
a: He wrote a letter refusing to hate the terrorists
He withdrew from public life permanently
He campaigned to ban social media platforms
He demanded revenge against the attackers
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes his open letter, You Will Not Have My Hate, pledging that he and his son would keep moving forward.
